ask: Survey memory-serving MCP servers first-hand: mem0, Letta/MemGPT MCP servers, knowledge-memory servers, and the localfirst-memory landscape (our 10-01 drop-dig at watch/inbox/localfirst_*). Who serves memory across MULTIPLE agents; how they scope/persist/auth. Start from: fetch each product's MCP docs.
method: curl raw bytes of each product's MCP docs (READMEs, Mintlify .md doc pages, llms.txt indexes) into fetched/ with a sha256 manifest (citation-resolution law: bytes or UNVERIFIED); all quotes byte-copied and grep-verified before writing; the localfirst surface read from the estate's own 10-01 dig receipts (watch/inbox/localfirst/adjacent.md, lbrain.md). No em-dash and no en-dash anywhere in this file (enforced by the check script).

GitHub API contents of mem0ai/mem0 mcp/ directory on main

servers.name: Mem0 hosted Platform MCP (docs.mem0.ai/platform/mem0-mcp)
servers.transport: remote HTTP at https://mcp.mem0.ai/mcp; one-click mcp-add for claude code, cursor, windsurf, vscode, opencode; Claude Desktop via Settings connector
servers.tools: 11: add_memory, search_memories, get_memories, get_memory, update_memory, delete_memory, delete_all_memories, delete_entities, list_entities, list_events, get_event_status (the last two are async-op status polling)
servers.scoping: entity taxonomy user/agent/app/run: delete_entities deletes a user/agent/app/run entity and its memories; list_entities enumerates users/agents/apps/runs stored in Mem0
servers.persistence: vendor cloud account: memories live in your Mem0 account, not on your computer
servers.auth: two paths: browser OAuth sign-in through the client (token stored and refreshed by the client), or API key as bearer token for headless/CI; neither means 401 Authentication required
servers.multi_agent: yes by construction: any MCP client on the same account shares the store, separated by the entity taxonomy; per-run isolation rides the run entity

servers.name: mem0-mcp-server (archived OSS wrapper, mem0ai/mem0-mcp)
servers.transport: three shapes: uvx stdio local package, Docker exposing an /mcp HTTP endpoint, Smithery remote hosted
servers.tools: 9 memory tools (same set as hosted minus list_events and get_event_status)
servers.scoping: MEM0_DEFAULT_USER_ID env var injects a default user_id into filters and write requests, defaulting to mem0-mcp; entity taxonomy user/agent/app/run preserved in tool args
servers.persistence: none of its own: it wraps the Mem0 Platform API, so storage is still the vendor cloud
servers.auth: MEM0_API_KEY required (platform key); the repo itself is now a public archive
servers.multi_agent: one default user per client config, so cross-agent sharing means sharing the same env default or passing explicit entity ids

servers.name: Letta hosted MCP server (docs.letta.com/platform/hosted-mcp)
servers.transport: remote HTTP at https://api.letta.com/mcp; applies_to backends: cloud only
servers.tools: 6, and none of them are memory CRUD: list_agents, list_models, create_agent, send_agent_message, get_run, get_reply; memory is served by serving the agents themselves
servers.scoping: agent identity plus conversation: pass agent_id to start a conversation, a conv-... conversation_id to continue one, or agent_id with conversation_id default; agents found by name, tags, or query
servers.persistence: Letta cloud holds agent memory; the calling agent does not resend context
servers.auth: bearer API key only; OAuth-only clients are not supported yet
servers.multi_agent: the sharpest multi-agent shape in the survey: any MCP client can create and message stateful Letta agents, and memory travels inside the agent, not in the caller
servers.risk_note: Messages run on a Cloud computer in unrestricted permission mode: the agent executes tools without approval prompts. That is the anti-posture for the estate effect model (switchboard/effect broker authorizes effects).

servers.name: Letta Agent SDK MCP consumption (docs.letta.com/agent-sdk/mcp)
servers.transport: inverse direction: Letta sessions consume MCP servers (stdio, Streamable HTTP, legacy SSE) from the SDK Node.js process; tools namespaced mcp__<server>__<tool>
servers.tools: not a memory server; this is a memory-hungry agent runtime attaching arbitrary MCP tool servers
servers.scoping: tools are scoped to the SDK session; different sessions on the same stateful agent may use different MCP servers and credentials
servers.persistence: MCP tools are not persisted on the Letta agent; implementations, processes, credentials, and filesystem access belong to the application hosting the session
servers.auth: bearer tokens via headers config; the SDK does not open an interactive OAuth browser flow

servers.name: Official MCP knowledge-graph memory server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory, modelcontextprotocol/servers src/memory)
servers.transport: local stdio via npx or docker; Windows needs cmd /c wrapper
servers.tools: 9 graph tools: create_entities, create_relations, add_observations, delete_entities, delete_observations, delete_relations, read_graph, search_nodes, open_nodes; plus a knowledge-graph MCP resource at memory://knowledge-graph whose mutations emit notifications/resources/updated so subscribed clients see live changes
servers.scoping: none enforced: user identity is a system-prompt convention telling the model to assume it is talking to default_user
servers.persistence: one JSONL file: MEMORY_FILE_PATH env var, default memory.jsonl in the server directory
servers.auth: none; it is a local stdio process with no account, no tokens, no network
servers.multi_agent: none built in: one stdio instance per client; cross-agent sharing only by pointing two clients at the same file path, with no concurrency or locking story in the README

servers.name: Cognee MCP (docs.cognee.ai/cognee-mcp/mcp-overview)
servers.transport: local via uvx/docker for standalone, or API mode pointing at a centralized Cognee backend
servers.tools: v1.0 memory trio remember, recall, forget (legacy lower-level tools remain); tools/list exposes a subset with the rest discoverable through tool search to keep payload small
servers.scoping: two modes: Standalone keeps each MCP instance's data separate; API Mode shares one knowledge graph across multiple MCP instances under one Cognee user (the docs flag what that means when several tenants share one deployment)
servers.persistence: standalone out of the box: SQLite, LanceDB, and the embedded Ladybug (Kuzu) graph store, switchable to Neo4j or Postgres; API mode: the centralized backend
servers.auth: standalone: none named on the overview page; API mode: a single token per instance
servers.multi_agent: the only surveyed server with an explicit named mode for several assistants sharing one knowledge graph

servers.name: Basic Memory (basicmachines-co/basic-memory, AGPL-3.0)
servers.transport: local stdio via uvx basic-memory mcp; cloud web app over https; also ChatGPT search/fetch actions and host-native plugins (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, and a namesake Hermes plugin that is not the estate's hermes-agent)
servers.tools: write_note, read_note, edit_note, move_note, delete_note, read_content, view_note; search_notes, recent_activity, list_directory; build_context navigating memory:// URLs; project tools list_memory_projects, create_memory_project, delete_project; schema_infer, schema_validate, schema_diff; every tool ships MCP behavior hints (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint)
servers.scoping: projects are the unit: per-project cloud routing via API key (bm project set-cloud) while other projects stay local; Teams is a single shared cloud workspace
servers.persistence: Markdown files plus a local SQLite index, default ~/basic-memory; cloud runs WorkOS AuthKit, Neon Postgres, and Tigris S3 with bidirectional rclone sync
servers.auth: local: none (plain files on disk); cloud: account via WorkOS; $15/mo cloud plan, BMFOSS discount
servers.multi_agent: Teams: anything a teammate writes is immediately available to everyone else and to their AI assistants; locally: humans and AIs write the same Markdown with sync conflict resolution

servers.name: OpenMemory (mem0ai/openmemory) PIVOTED
servers.transport: CLI and TUI installer, not an MCP server
servers.tools: n/a: it ports conversation sessions between coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode now; OpenClaw, Hermes on the roadmap)
servers.scoping: session ids per harness; omni-directional import/export with preview
servers.persistence: per-harness session stores on your machine
servers.multi_agent: no: this is one developer syncing their own session history across harness front-ends
servers.pivot_note: The May 2025 OpenMemory framing (local-first MCP memory layer) is gone from the repo front door; the current README pitches session sync. Any estate brief citing OpenMemory as a memory MCP server is stale and must be re-tri-stated.

servers.name: LBrain (metavolve-labs/lbrain, from the estate 10-01 dig, estate file watch/inbox/localfirst/lbrain.md)
servers.transport: CLI plus FastMCP stdio server, 6 tools and 1 resource; ai.lbrain/lbrain on pypi/uvx
servers.scoping: persona is env-only and binds to transport, never to a tool argument, after red-team finding 12: a model that could pass persona='cfo' could read the CFO's private working memory by asking nicely; the fix is that provider and persona selection come from explicit init and nowhere else
servers.persistence: local lairs, FTS5 exact search verb separate from hybrid BM25 plus sqlite-vec fused search verb
servers.auth: no account by default: an unregistered brain is a first-class state; unconfigured installs fail toward on-device, never toward a hosted provider
servers.multi_agent: single-user local by posture; the persona-transport binding is the transferable law

servers.name: GroundMemory and people-context (tiny SQLite MCP memory servers, from estate 10-01 dig watch/inbox/localfirst/adjacent.md)
servers.persistence: one SQLite file per product; GroundMemory adds FTS5 and a Markdown mirror of the graph

scoping_models: entity taxonomy user/agent/app/run under a vendor account: mem0 hosted and its archived wrapper
agent identity plus conversation id: Letta hosted MCP server (memory lives in stateful agents, served as MCP tools)
project or workspace: Basic Memory (per-project local/cloud routing; Teams shared workspace); Cognee standalone per-instance
one token one user: Cognee API mode (the docs themselves flag the multi-tenant caveat)
none, identity by prompt convention: official knowledge-graph memory server, GroundMemory, people-context
identity via transport binding, not tool args: LBrain (estate 10-01 dig)
matrix.persistence_spectrum: vendor cloud (mem0, Letta cloud, Basic Memory cloud, Cognee API mode) at one end; local files with indexes at the other (JSONL knowledge graph; Markdown plus SQLite; SQLite plus LanceDB plus Kuzu; SQLite FTS5)
matrix.auth_spectrum: OAuth-or-bearer (mem0 hosted), bearer-only (Letta hosted), single token (Cognee API mode), none local (official memory server, Basic Memory local, LBrain)
matrix.multi_agent_answer: Four shapes actually serve memory across multiple agents: (1) mem0 hosted, shared account with entity taxonomy; (2) Letta hosted, memory inside stateful agents served as MCP tools; (3) Cognee API mode, multiple MCP instances on one shared knowledge graph; (4) Basic Memory Teams, shared cloud workspace. Everything local-first and single-file serves exactly one agent per instance and calls it memory, with no auth and no concurrency story.

landscape_shifts_vs_10_01_bank: mem0: the OSS MCP wrapper mem0-mcp-server is now a public archive per its README caution; the MCP surface mem0 offers is the hosted server at mcp.mem0.ai. The 10-01 adjacent.md row (mem0 memory-infrastructure API with self-host SUPPORTED, from the main README) is still true for the library, but the MCP layer specifically is hosted-only now.

OpenMemory: pivoted from local-first MCP memory layer to session-sync across coding harnesses; the mem0ai/openmemory main README is the session-sync product. Prior briefs citing the May 2025 framing are stale.

Letta: docs now show two MCP surfaces (hosted MCP server exposing agents as tools; Agent SDK consuming MCP servers); this rides on top of the 10-01 finding that letta main README is a stub handing off to letta-code with MemFS git-tracked context.
Basic Memory: now sells a Teams shared-cloud workspace tier and per-project cloud routing on top of the AGPL local core; the hybrid local-plus-cloud-per-project shape is new since the 10-01 bank.

steal_rows.claim: Basic Memory annotates every MCP tool with read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world hints so agents pick the right tool without trial-and-error, and Codex-class clients key their approval flows off the destructive hint.
steal_rows.steal: Add readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint annotations to every estate MCP verb at spec time (R2 memory verbs in the bridge spec; estate_corpus_search read-only, any future write verb destructive); landing spot mag/estate_bridge.py BRIDGE_INPUT_SCHEMAS spec block.
steal_rows.falsifier: Estate bridge clients demonstrably ignore annotations, so the hints change no behavior anywhere.

steal_rows.law: scope binds to transport identity, never to a model-passable argument
steal_rows.claim: Every surveyed multi-agent memory surface binds scope to credentials or account entities (bearer key, one token one user, account entities), and none binds it to a schema string the model can pass; LBrain learned this the hard way (red-team finding 12).
steal_rows.steal: In the R2 memory verbs spec, keep seat scope bound to the R3 bridge token; never accept a scope/user_id argument from the model; cite LBrain and the Cognee one-token-one-user caveat as precedent in the spec.
steal_rows.falsifier: A major server shipping enforced per-call scope strings that actually isolate tenants.

steal_rows.law: live graph reads can be resources with change notifications
steal_rows.claim: The official knowledge-graph memory server exposes the whole graph as a memory://knowledge-graph resource and emits notifications/resources/updated on every mutation so subscribed clients see live changes.
steal_rows.steal: Candidate shape for estate bonds/corpus reads on the house bridge: expose the read surface as an MCP resource with resource-updated notifications when the percolator or seed-seal mutates; only if a bridge client can actually subscribe.
steal_rows.falsifier: No estate MCP client can subscribe to resource notifications (stdio request-response bridge), then the shape is dead weight.

steal_rows.law: hosted memory is off-machine by default and unauthenticated callers get 401
steal_rows.claim: Mem0's official MCP server runs nothing locally, holds memories in the vendor account, and answers unauthenticated calls with 401 Authentication required.
steal_rows.steal: Fix the estate posture in the bridge spec: memory stays local-first; hosted-memory MCP is a named fallback shape only, with bearer-key auth and explicit account-scoping if ever crossed.
steal_rows.falsifier: A hosted memory provider shipping a first-class local persistence mode equal to its cloud mode.

steal_rows.law: agent-cloud execution without approvals is the anti-posture
steal_rows.claim: Letta's hosted MCP server runs messages on a cloud computer in unrestricted permission mode where the agent executes tools without approval prompts.
steal_rows.steal: Use as the named counter-example in the bridge/effect-broker spec: the estate rule is that model text proposes and the switchboard/effect broker authorizes effects, never an unrestricted remote execution mode.
steal_rows.falsifier: Letta shipping per-tool approval gates as the default for hosted MCP-driven agent execution.

steal_rows.law: single-file no-auth memory is single-user by construction
steal_rows.claim: The official MCP memory server persists one JSONL file, enforces no identity, and relies on a prompt convention telling the model to assume the user is default_user.
steal_rows.steal: Reject single-file no-auth memory servers for any multi-seat estate surface; the estate's sha256-pinned FTS5 corpus search already exceeds them on determinism and citation-resolvability.
steal_rows.falsifier: The reference server shipping enforced per-user namespaces or locking.

steal_rows.law: async memory operations get status surfaces
steal_rows.claim: Mem0's hosted MCP tool list includes list_events and get_event_status so an agent can poll the status of an async memory operation by event_id.
steal_rows.steal: If estate bridge writes ever cross (percolator candidates, seed seal), pair each write verb with an event row and a get_status read verb instead of long-blocking calls.
steal_rows.falsifier: Estate writes stay synchronous and bounded, then the status surface is unneeded; revisit only when a write crosses the bridge.

quotes.text: Nothing runs on your machine: the server is hosted by Mem0, and your client connects to it over HTTPS.
Memories you store this way live in your Mem0 account, not on your computer.
If neither is set up, the server replies `401 Authentication required` and your client reports the connection as failed.
**mem0-mcp-server** is no longer actively maintained and this repository is now a public archive.
Bulk delete all memories in the confirmed scope (user/agent/app/run).
Letta agents keep their memory across every conversation, so the calling agent does not need to resend context.
The client must support custom bearer headers; OAuth-only clients are not supported yet.
Messages run on a Cloud computer in unrestricted permission mode: the agent executes tools without approval prompts.
They are not persisted on the Letta agent: their implementations, processes, credentials, and filesystem access belong to the application hosting the session.
A basic implementation of persistent memory using a local knowledge graph. This lets Claude remember information about the user across chats.
`MEMORY_FILE_PATH`: Path to the memory storage JSONL file (default: `memory.jsonl` in the server directory)
You should assume that you are interacting with default_user
emit `notifications/resources/updated` for this URI, so subscribed clients see live changes
Run it standalone for one user, or in [API Mode](#architecture-modes) so several assistants share one knowledge graph.
Each instance authenticates with a single token, so everything it writes belongs to one Cognee user
Out of the box it uses SQLite, LanceDB, and the embedded Ladybug (Kuzu) graph store
Developers feel locked in to their primary harness, unable to try new ones without losing all their context from previous sessions.
**Local-first.** Plain text on your disk. Forever.
Just files plus a local SQLite index. No servers required.
**Per-project cloud routing.** Route individual projects through the cloud
Give your team a single, shared cloud workspace. Knowledge isn't confined to one person
MCP behavior hints (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world)
an unregistered brain is a first-class state, not an error. Identity accretes onto an anonymous install; it never gates one.
One SQLite file on your machine. No account, no cloud, no network calls.
Just testing? Use the library. Building for a team? Self-hosted. Want zero ops? Cloud.
